sources.entry: Gas Mask - Simple hosts file manager for Mac OS X. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/2ndalpha/gasmask)
Gas Mask - Hosts file manager for macOS.

summary.one_liner: Gas Mask is a simple macOS app for managing and switching between hosts files, including local, remote, and combined hosts files.
summary.what_it_does: Gas Mask edits the /etc/hosts file on macOS and lets you switch between multiple hosts files. It runs in the background with a menu bar icon for quick switching and opens a main editor window with a list of hosts files and a text editor. Local files can be edited directly, while remote files are downloaded from URLs and synchronized on a schedule set in Preferences (they cannot be edited). Combined files hold a list of local and remote files rather than raw entries. Activating a file overwrites /etc/hosts with the chosen file, and the active file name can be shown in the status bar. Custom files are stored in ~/Library/Gas Mask, and logs are written to ~/Library/Logs/Gas Mask.log.
use_cases: Switch between different hosts file profiles on a Mac
Block ads or trackers via a remote hosts list
Combine several local and remote hosts lists into one active file
how_to_run: Download the latest version (0.8.6) from the project's README link
Drag the application from Downloads into the Applications folder
Launch the app and enter your password when prompted, so it can modify /etc/hosts
Build from source with Xcode 15 or later, if preferred
notable: Combined files merge local and remote hosts lists into one active file
Remote hosts files sync automatically on a configurable interval
Menu bar icon for quick switching without opening the editor
caveats: Needs administrator password because it modifies /etc/hosts
Remote files are read-only and get overwritten on each update
